To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. We present the first compression method for deep neural networks that can be applied to a large variety of network architectures, including convolutional and recurrent networks, and that can achieve state-of-the-art compression
(1) atomic networks can be trained with backpropagation, (2) the resulting networks can be used to perform inference, and (3) the resulting networks are smaller than their uncompressed counterparts.
1. We propose to train the model using a new objective function called the atomic gradient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of compressed neural networks.
the design of deep neural networks with low computational complexity, and with efficient training methods for these networks.
the design of deep neural network architectures for the purpose of improving performance on a wide variety of computer vision tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the atomic compression technique in the context of deep neural networks has been shown to be a very effective and efficient way of compressing and deploying deep neural networks.
, in general, it is not possible to compress a deep network by using the same number of parameters.
the current state-of-the-art in the field of deep learning is to use the ResNet architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the atomic compression networks (ACN), proposed by our group, is a new framework that combines the merits of both knowledge distillation and quantization, and achieves the best trade-off between the accuracy and the compression ratio.
we can use a deep neural network to learn a compression network that can be used to compress any other deep neural network.
the proposed atomic compression networks (ACNs) are able to learn a compact and accurate model with a significantly lower parameter count.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the compression rate of the network can be improved significantly by adding more parameters, which is in contrast with the conventional wisdom that the compression rate is a monotonically increasing function of the number of parameters.

, in order to achieve state-of-the-art performance in image classification with a small model size, we need to use the full expressiveness of the network architecture and train it with large batch sizes and high momentum.
we can achieve state-of-the-art performance on a variety of computer vision tasks using a single model that is 1000x smaller than the original network.
